title: CNC drilling machine hydraulic requirements
scope_statement: Validated scope: generic hydraulic component classes, functional valve behavior, and direct port-to-port connectivity only. Pump/cylinder/reservoir sizing, pressure and flow ratings, line selection, filtration, cooling, prime mover selection, simulation and fabrication approval are explicitly deferred to the later sizing and engineering phases.
design_narrative: Open-circuit fixed-displacement hydraulic topology with a shared open-centre 4/3 DCV commanding both clamp and drill branches. The clamp branch is connected through a dual pilot-operated check/load-lock at the clamp actuator ports. Forward drill feed is pressure-permitted by an externally piloted sequence valve sensing the clamp extend supply line, and drill extension speed is controlled by a single non-compensated one-way flow control in the drill rod-end exhaust meter-out path. Reverse operation sends drill retract flow through the one-way flow control free-flow direction while clamp release is blocked by a second externally piloted sequence valve until drill retract pressure rises. All relief, DCV return, and sequence-valve drains return directly to Tank.R; no manifold, tee, hose, filter, gauge, motor, coupling, or electrical interface is introduced.

selected_components.name: Tank
selected_components.role: open-circuit reservoir for suction and all returns/drains

selected_components.name: Pump
selected_components.selection_basis: No efficiency or standby unloading requirement overrides the directive to prefer a fixed-displacement pump.

selected_components.name: Relief Valve
configuration: pressure limit setting deferred to sizing for the specified maximum system pressure
selected_components.selection_basis: Required to limit maximum hydraulic system pressure.

selected_components.name: 4/3 Solenoid DCV, Open Center
selected_components.role: shared extend/neutral/retract command valve for the clamp and drill sequence
configuration: extend state supplies the forward/clamp/drill-feed command branch
retract state supplies the drill-retract and gated clamp-release command branch
neutral unloads pump and vents work lines to tank
selected_components.selection_basis: One shared DCV satisfies hydraulic sequencing directive; open centre suits a fixed pump while venting pilot-check pilot lines.

selected_components.name: Double-Acting Cylinder
configuration: double acting; geometry and stroke deferred to sizing
selected_components.selection_basis: Bidirectional linear motion is required for clamp extend and retract.

selected_components.name: Double-Acting Cylinder
configuration: double acting; geometry and stroke deferred to sizing
selected_components.selection_basis: Bidirectional linear motion is required for drill feed extend and retract.

selected_components.name: Dual Pilot-Operated Check Valve
selected_components.role: low-leakage clamp holding and commanded hydraulic release
configuration: installed at clamp actuator work ports
cross-piloted release from the opposite commanded line
selected_components.selection_basis: The clamp must retain the workpiece during drilling and until release is hydraulically permitted; DCV spool leakage alone is not acceptable.

selected_components.name: Externally Piloted Sequence Valve with Reverse Check
selected_components.role: hydraulic permissive for drill feed after clamp pressure condition
configuration: closed until external pilot from clamp supply/pressure condition opens the drill-feed branch
reverse check preserves drill return path
selected_components.selection_basis: Drilling must begin only after clamp reaches the workpiece and develops the required hydraulic pressure condition without electrical sensing.

selected_components.name: One-Way Speed Control
selected_components.role: adjustable non-compensated meter-out control for drill extension feed
configuration: metered A-to-B path used from drill rod chamber exhaust to return during drill extension
free reverse B-to-A path allows drill retract supply to the rod chamber
selected_components.selection_basis: Typed drill_extend_feed decision requires exactly one non-compensated one-way flow control in the rod-chamber exhaust meter-out path.

selected_components.name: Externally Piloted Sequence Valve with Reverse Check
selected_components.role: hydraulic reverse-order interlock for clamp release after drill retract
configuration: external pilot senses drill retract pressure rise at retract end condition
opens clamp release/retract supply and clamp load-lock release path
selected_components.selection_basis: Clamp release must remain unavailable until drill retraction condition is satisfied, using hydraulic rather than electrical sequencing.

motion_control_decisions.justification: Numeric speed and force targets are sizing requirements only; authoritative clarification says the phase is resistive/non-overrunning, so no dynamic load-control capability is required during powered extension.
The clamp must retain the workpiece while drilling and before release is allowed; this is a static retention requirement rather than an overrunning-motion control requirement.

Release return has no specified controlled speed target and no retention requirement after release; authoritative clarification says the phase is resistive/non-overrunning, so no dynamic load-control capability is required.

Numeric feed speed and drilling force are sizing requirements only; authoritative clarification says the load is resistive/non-overrunning and no load-independent or adjustable speed requirement was stated.
Return speed and force are not specified; authoritative clarification says the phase is resistive/non-overrunning, so no dynamic load-control capability is required.

function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Tank.S supplies Pump.S; Pump.P branches directly to ReliefValve.P and DCV.P; ReliefValve.T and DCV.T return directly to Tank.R. Relief setting and pump displacement are deferred to sizing.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: shared-command clamp-first pressure sequence with pilot-check holding and reverse sequence release
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: DCV extend supplies the clamp cap through ClampLoadLock A1-A2 first. The dual pilot-operated check provides low-leakage clamp holding. Clamp release/retraction is supplied only after ReverseSequenceValve opens from drill retract pressure, then ReverseSequenceValve.A supplies ClampLoadLock.B1 and the clamp rod chamber while the opposite pilot releases cap exhaust to DCV.A/Tank.

ForwardSequenceValve opens from clamp supply pressure and supplies DrillCylinder.Cap for drill extension. DrillCylinder.Rod exhaust is routed through DrillFeedFlowControl A-to-B before returning to DCV.B, implementing the declared adjustable non-compensated meter-out path. DCV retract supplies DrillCylinder.Rod through the one-way flow control free reverse path and the resulting retract pressure pilots ReverseSequenceValve for subsequent clamp release.

design_decisions.decision: Use one shared open-centre 4/3 DCV for clamp and drill sequencing.
design_decisions.rationale: One shared directional valve keeps clamp and drill branches simultaneously referenced to the same hydraulic command, so sequence-valve ordering is hydraulic rather than a result of independent electrical valve timing. Open-centre neutral also suits the fixed-displacement pump and vents work lines for pilot-check reseating.

design_decisions.decision: Use fixed-displacement open-circuit pump supply with relief protection.
design_decisions.rationale: The selected power path provides the required open-circuit hydraulic supply and a direct relief return to the reservoir for pressure limiting; displacement and relief setting remain sizing tasks.

design_decisions.decision: Install a dual pilot-operated check/load lock at the clamp actuator ports.
design_decisions.rationale: The clamp must retain the workpiece during drilling and release only when hydraulically commanded. A dual load lock blocks unintended reverse flow at both clamp cylinder chambers and is cross-released by pressure on the opposite commanded line.

design_decisions.decision: Gate drill feed through an externally piloted forward sequence valve piloted from the clamp extend supply line.
design_decisions.rationale: The drill feed branch is blocked until clamp supply pressure reaches the permissive threshold, and its pilot is taken from the clamp actuator supply condition rather than the common pump line.

design_decisions.decision: Place exactly one one-way flow control in the drill rod-end exhaust meter-out path.
design_decisions.rationale: The typed drill_extend_feed decision requires adjustable, non-compensated meter-out control on rod-chamber exhaust. The selected path DrillCylinder.Rod to DrillFeedFlowControl.A to DrillFeedFlowControl.B to DCV.B implements that requirement without a parallel bypass.

design_decisions.decision: Use a second externally piloted sequence valve for reverse-order clamp release after drill retract.
design_decisions.rationale: DCV retract supplies the drill rod side immediately and supplies clamp release only through ReverseSequenceValve. The valve opens on drill retract-line pressure rise, implementing the required drill-retract-before-clamp-release interlock with catalog-available hydraulic components.

assumptions: Relief pressure, sequence thresholds, pump displacement, actuator bore/rod/stroke, and flow-control setting are sizing selections and are not fixed by this topology.
The reverse release permissive is assumed to be the drill retract-line pressure rise that occurs when the drill cylinder reaches its retracted end stop.
The open-centre DCV neutral vents A and B to tank, allowing pilot-check release pressure to decay so the clamp load lock can reseat.
The selected externally piloted sequence valve's integral reverse check is used for reverse return paths; no separate plain check valve is added.
open_issues: Sizing must set the relief and sequence thresholds and select actuator and pump dimensions.
The assumed drill-retracted confirmation is a retract-line pressure rise at the end stop and should be validated for the machine duty cycle.
Final detailed netlist must ensure no unmetered bypass is simultaneously open around the drill feed flow control during extension.
No cited standard was supplied for hydraulic machinery safety, verification, guarding, or fluid-power design practice; standards review remains open before final machine release.
Sequence phase 'drill_retract_return' omits expected active functions ['workpiece_clamp'].

The drill_retract_return phase declares only drill_feed active and explicitly lists workpiece_clamp as forbidden, but the brief requires the clamp to retain the workpiece until clamp release is hydraulically permitted after drill retraction. During drill retract the clamp holding function must remain an active required state, even though the clamp is not moving. This failed phase invariant leaves acceptance coverage for 'prevent clamp release before drill retract return condition is satisfied' inconsistent with the required sequence.

research_coverage.summary: The evidence is sufficient for the basic open hydraulic power/return/relief topology, double-acting cylinder directional-control principles, clamp load-holding with pilot-operated check/lock valves, and clamp-pressure-before-drill-feed sequencing. It is not yet sufficient to design the full requested topology safely and unambiguously because two critical areas remain under-supported: the drill feed’s specified adjustable meter-out speed control at the rod exhaust during extension, and the positive interlock that prevents clamp release until drill return is confirmed.

items.rationale: Findings provide cited connection guidance for an open-loop circuit: reservoir to pump suction, pump pressure to valves/actuators, return to reservoir, and relief/diversion to tank. Open-center/tandem-center unloading for fixed-displacement pumps is also supported by cited technical sources.

Findings support double-acting cylinder control using 4-way/3-position directional valves, shifted P-A/B-T or P-B/A-T flow paths, and neutral-center implications. Clamp-specific safety is addressed by adding pilot-operated check/lock valves rather than relying on spool neutral leakage.

Basic extend/hold/retract phases are supported by double-acting cylinder directional control and pilot-check holding. Clamp-pressure-before-drill transition is supported by sequence-valve evidence. However, the accumulated evidence is still weak for the complete automatic release-side transition logic because clamp release must be inhibited until drill return is confirmed, and no strong source yet gives port-level interlock logic for that condition.

Cited textbook/manufacturer/technical evidence supports that blocked DCV ports can leak and allow cylinder creep, and that pilot-operated check/double lock valves block cylinder flow in neutral and release by cross-pilot pressure. This covers the load-holding and controlled-release pattern for the clamp actuator.

Findings support using a double-acting hydraulic cylinder with a 4-way directional valve for extend/retract, including shifted port connections and neutral-center behavior. That is enough for the directional-control portion of drill-feed topology.

Extend/retract directional actuation is supported, but the specified drill feed profile requires adjustable throttled meter-out speed control at the rod exhaust during extension. The accumulated findings do not provide cited engineering guidance for flow-control valve type, meter-out versus meter-in rationale, or placement on the rod-end exhaust line for extension speed control.

Clamp-before-drill-feed sequencing is supported by cited sequence-valve evidence: a normally closed pressure-sensing valve opens a downstream branch only after a preset pressure is reached. However, the required multi-actuator interlock is incomplete because no strong source supports a positive drill-return-before-unclamp interlock, such as a hydraulic limit valve, sequence valve arrangement, pressure switch, or pilot-release logic tied to drill-return confirmation.

Clamp force retention during drilling is well supported by pilot-operated check/double lock valve evidence and warnings against relying on spool leakage. The need also states that the clamp must not release until drill return permits release; that release-permission interlock is not yet supported by strong cited connection logic.

Evidence supports a pressure relief valve branch from pump pressure to tank/return as the pressure-limiting topology. The 8 bar value is a design requirement to apply as the relief setting/selection criterion; the evidence need is topology, not validating the user-specified numerical limit.

missing_or_weak_information: Missing critical claim: an adjustable flow-control/throttle valve should be placed in the drill-feed cylinder exhaust path for meter-out speed control during extension, specifically on the rod-end exhaust branch when the cap end is pressurized for extension, or equivalent cited guidance clarifying correct placement for the chosen cylinder orientation.

Missing critical claim: a hydraulic or electrohydraulic interlock method can positively prevent clamp release until the drill-feed actuator has returned, with supported component classes and connection/placement logic, e.g. a mechanically actuated limit valve, pressure switch, pilot-operated valve, or sequencing arrangement tied to drill-return confirmation.

Weak but probably nonblocking: existing pilot-check evidence supports load holding and cross-pilot release, but does not explicitly state all neutral pilot-line venting requirements for every possible DCV center condition. Final design should ensure the selected neutral condition cannot leave release pilot pressure trapped.

design_issues.description: The drill_retract_return phase declares only drill_feed active and explicitly lists workpiece_clamp as forbidden, but the brief requires the clamp to retain the workpiece until clamp release is hydraulically permitted after drill retraction. During drill retract the clamp holding function must remain an active required state, even though the clamp is not moving. This failed phase invariant leaves acceptance coverage for 'prevent clamp release before drill retract return condition is satisfied' inconsistent with the required sequence.

The reverse-order interlock topology is plausible and uses the available sequence_valve class, but the supplied research notes weak direct evidence for the exact pattern of using drill retract end-stop pressure to open a clamp-release sequence valve. This does not by itself prevent the requested behavior, but it should be backed by targeted schematic/reference evidence before final release.

design_review.summary: The hydraulic component selection and main directed paths are largely consistent with the brief: open-circuit pump/relief supply, one shared DCV, clamp pilot-check holding, forward clamp-pressure sequence for drill feed, rod-end meter-out drill feed control, and a reverse sequence valve for clamp release. However, the declared drill_retract_return phase violates the required clamp-retention invariant by omitting/forbidding the active clamp hold state while the drill retracts. Because that phase coverage contradicts the required return order and holding behavior, the topology package is invalid until the phase model is corrected.
